I think your 4 year old might really like it if you're helping him a long just a bit, it really doesn't have to be too hard, the reason some of the videos you watch take hundreds of hours is because they are doing them at like 24 frames per second, but in all honesty you can get away with doing like 8 frames a second, and if its just you and your 4 year old starting out you could get away with very few, but once you make a video or two you become more comfortable in your movements and can move through them pretty quickly.

If your 4 year old was with you just try and make it fun, use his action figures/legos/toys whatever you want and just ask him what he wants to see them do, if he's watching you move everything and then actually see's it come to life playing through the camera he might really get into it, I was actually teaching my 5 year old cousin how to do it with his moms camera, we were just using some of his toy cars and tractors making them drive around and just do stuff, I feel like every kid just wants to see their toys come to life at some point!

So don't worry too much about quality, the basics would just be a tripod to keep everything nice and steady, I would also highly recommend a camera remote if you have a DSLR like this: http://ecx.images-amazon.com/images/I/41QVWJJBECL.jpg

for a program you can just use windows movie maker to put the pictures together and play in a video format, It also comes with all versions of windows (you just have to download the window's live essentials) which you can just find by searching the programs tab in the start menu.
